paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Beekeeping is no longer only a countryside activity. In the last ten years, thousands of people have started keeping bees on the roofs of offices, hotels and apartment blocks in cities around the world.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: One reason for this trend is that cities can actually be better for bees than farmland. Large farms often grow a single crop and spray chemicals, whereas city gardens, parks and balconies offer a wide variety of flowers that bloom at different times of the year. As a result, urban bees tend to produce honey throughout the whole summer.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: However, experts warn that the boom may be creating a new problem. When too many hives are placed in the same area, honeybees compete with wild bee species for a limited amount of food, and some of those wild species, which are far better at pollinating native plants, may decline. Rather than adding more hives, some researchers argue, cities would do more good by planting flowers that support all kinds of pollinators.

question_groups.instruction: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.
